kind: bounded primary-source comparison, not exhaustive novelty proof

papers.title: VUS: effective and efficient accuracy measures for time-series anomaly detection
papers.already_established: Defines and optimizes VUS with static/dynamic work reuse and threshold/runtime sensitivity.
papers.distinction: Preserve the operator while compressing exhaustive complete-tie support events and sharing label work across model scores; fast VUS and reuse themselves are not new.

papers.title: PATE: Proximity-Aware Time series anomaly Evaluation
papers.already_established: Introduces proximity-weighted PR evaluation and analyzes buffer-size/complexity effects.
papers.distinction: Computing a fixed existing VUS target more cheaply differs from proposing a different utility metric; do not claim novel weighted PR.

papers.title: The Elephant in the Room: Towards A Reliable Time-Series Anomaly Detection Benchmark
papers.already_established: TSB-AD evaluates 40 algorithms and 1070 series, studies metric reliability and recommends VUS-PR.
papers.distinction: This work studies exact computational fidelity/cost of that evaluator, not a new detector benchmark or another general ranking audit.

papers.title: TAB: Unified Benchmarking of Time Series Anomaly Detection Methods
papers.already_established: Unified data, method, evaluation layers; diverse metrics and standardized preprocessing and strategies.
papers.distinction: A shared-label exact operator is a component optimization; the pipeline concept and scalable benchmarking are prior work.

papers.title: TSB-AutoAD: Towards Automated Solutions for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
papers.already_established: Evaluates selection, ensembling and generation methods, including their accuracy/efficiency trade-offs.
papers.distinction: Labeled offline selection cost and numerical fidelity are distinct from learning an unlabeled deployment selector; no AutoML superiority is asserted.

papers.title: Formally Exploring Time-Series Anomaly Detection Evaluation Metrics
papers.already_established: Analyzes 37 metrics and proposes LARM/ALARM; section3 explicitly excludes score-based volume-under-surface metrics from the formal analysis.
papers.distinction: The target here is an existing score-integrated dynamic metric, with complete-tie computation rather than new metric axioms.

papers.title: CCE: Confidence-Consistency Evaluation for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.relevance: Fast alternative metric and ranking evaluation
papers.already_established: Proposes confidence/consistency scores, an O(n) computation and RankEval.
papers.distinction: A different O(n) metric cannot be treated as a same-output baseline; preserve the existing VUS target and compare matched operators.

papers.title: A Problem-Oriented Taxonomy of Evaluation Metrics for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.already_established: Organizes metrics by application needs including tolerance, timeliness, random-score robustness and audit costs.
papers.distinction: Separate semantic choice from approximation of one declared target; do not rebrand a metric taxonomy or ranking change as novel.

papers.title: Did We Actually Fix It? An Independent Adversarial Stress-Test of Post-Point-Adjustment Evaluation Metrics for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
papers.already_established: Studies best-of-N no-skill reporting on six benchmarks and inter-metric rank agreement with VUS resolution250.
papers.distinction: Our discrepancy holds scores/labels/metric fixed and changes numerical threshold integration; not a new seed-shopping or general metric-robustness result.

papers.title: Retrieval Over Training: Similarity search-based Model Selection for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.already_established: RAMSAD uses retrieval of historical detector profiles for model selection and reports OOD/runtime trade-offs.
papers.distinction: The new workload computes exact labeled profile scores; it does not replace the retrieval selector or claim better deployment accuracy.

papers.title: Fast or Accurate? Rethinking Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.already_established: Discusses fast CPU/GPU evaluation and model-selection cost.
papers.distinction: Credit efficient VUS as established; compare the actual pinned FF-VUS native contract separately rather than claiming it computes the original square-root target.

papers.title: mTSBench: Benchmarking Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection and Model Selection at Scale
papers.already_established: Public benchmark spans 344 multivariate series, 19 datasets, 24 detectors and model selection.
papers.distinction: Eight CPU detectors on univariate components are a targeted operator workload, not broader coverage than mTSBench; future claims need broader panels.

software_not_counted_as_papers: Sparse VUS v0.3.0 public unrefereed precursor
surviving_claim: A support-event representation preserves the pinned exhaustive dynamic VUS operator and complete global ties; its collection implementation reuses label-dependent width geometry across stored detector outputs. Standard sorting, loop interchange, caching, model selection and PR approximation warnings are not individually new.
